title: Rupert Cole the reed fanatic
summary: Cole played beautifully but threw away reed after reed, never satisfied, which Holmes teased him about.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I understand he was a bit of a perfectionist regarding reeds and things. Which I guess happens to many saxophonists.

Oh, yeah, with the reeds. Oh yeah. Well, he would play something, and it would be so beautiful. You'd just sit back and look at him with admiration. He was playing so beautiful and with such ease, you know. and then, when he gets through, he tears the reed off the horn and throws it away, and gets another one and starts chopping it down and trying it and this-that-and-the-other. And I come to find out this man is a fanatic about a reed! No reed ever satisfied him. And I don't know what he's trying to get out of a reed. He's playin' beautiful, his tone is big and broad and smooth and everything else. And I don't know what he's looking for in a reed, unless he wants one to play by itself. I used to kid him about it al the time. He'd say, 'No, these reed ain't just no good; no good. I'd
say, 'Well, as long as it makes a sound, it's all right with me.'
